title: Headwise dequant minimizer and prefill harmonizer
creator: Anika Sharma
description: Reduce per-request dequantization overhead for mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) attention kernels by introducing headwise hybrid execution and a prefill harmonizer that coalesces KV prefill for mixed-precision lanes. The goal is to reduce additional latency and memory copies introduced when switching precision on the critical prefill path while keeping model quality within tolerated deltas. This ticket scopes design, prototype kernel, microbenchmarks, and a small controlled rollout on internal dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype headwise hybrid kernel that executes attention QKV in mixed-precision without full-frame dequant copies
Prefill harmonizer reduces extra memcpy/dequant phases by >= 40% for common prefix lengths in our production traces
End-to-end per-request latency improvement of at least 8% on 8k sequence synthetic prefill benchmarks compared to current mixed-precision fallback path
No measurable degrade in generation quality (perplexity delta < 0.5% on validation prompts) and < 1% token-level regressions on customer prompt set A
Instrumentation and traces available in Console for per-token cost and per-model path split; rollout guarded by runtime flag and canary policy
tasks: Design headwise hybrid execution plan and API hooks for kernel selection
Implement prototype in runtime: headwise kernel wrapper + per-head precision mask
Add prefill harmonizer that merges contiguous prefill segments to minimize precision switches
Add telemetry: path counters, memcpy counts, token-level latency buckets
Run microbenchmarks across model families (7B, 13B, 70B) and representative batch sizes
Prepare canary rollout config and rollback hooks for Dedicated pools
benchmarks: Baseline mixed-precision fallback (current): median prefill latency 24.8ms @ batch=8 seq=2048 on A100
Prototype headwise hybrid: median prefill latency 22.6ms @ batch=8 seq=2048 (9% improvement)
Memcopy counts reduced: baseline 3 copies per request -> prototype 1 copy for typical 512-token prefixes
Cost estimate: expected token compute cost reduction ~6% due to fewer dequant ops in steady-state workloads
decisions: Use headwise precision mask rather than per-layer global precision switching to avoid full-tensor dequant
Prioritize prefill harmonizer heuristics that coalesce adjacent KV prefill segments when head precision matches
Fallback to safe full dequant path if telemetry detects >2% quality regression during canary
Expose runtime flag and Console toggle for per-customer opt-in during initial rollout
risks: Headwise execution increases code complexity and maintenance surface for kernels across backends
Risk of subtle numerical regressions when mixing INT8 and FP8 per-head — requires careful validation
Prefill harmonizer heuristics might worsen latency for pathological prefix shapes; must measure distribution impact
GPU memory alignment and bank conflicts may change with headwise packing — more perf tuning required
